items.notes: Netflix Chaos Kong case covers regional-failure testing and application-level failover; excerpt has no embedded SQLite or networked database-service content, so it does not address the question.
Database-design volume landing page; broad schema/storage scope is relevant background, but the excerpt exposes no document-embedding or record-lifecycle content.
Netflix cloud-rearchitecture case is a different timeline and architecture account; excerpt says nothing about Chaos Kong's tested failure envelope.
Multi-region disaster-recovery and restore-contract chapter directly covers failover, fencing and lost-commit restore concerns named in the question.
Same multi-region DR and restore-contract chapter covers failback and the conditions for an old region regaining authority.
Logs/audit/lineage record-semantics page covers which record kinds answer which questions; excerpt has no reservation workflow or notification-versus-business-success content.
Architecture-styles chapter on modules, services and ownership boundaries directly addresses the boundary-versus-deployment-unit distinction.
Sagas and transaction-isolation page concerns cross-service transactions; 'boundary' there is a service boundary, not a boundary register of design unknowns.
Object-permission and credentials page squarely addresses object-level resource authorization beyond an authenticated tenant identity.
Broad security-architecture page includes isolation, so it is relevant supporting context, but the excerpt does not show connection-pool or shared-resource tenant isolation.
